contentBlocks.text: You've found and evaluated sources. Today: take notes the right way, without copying someone else's words!

Plagiarism means presenting someone else's words or ideas as your own. Paraphrasing means restating an idea in your own words while still crediting the source — that's the honest way to take notes. Read this sentence: 'Rising ocean temperatures are causing coral reefs to lose their color in a process called bleaching.' Now paraphrase it in your own words, without copying the exact phrasing.
You just practiced honest paraphrasing, avoiding plagiarism! Tomorrow we'll organize research findings into an outline.

objectives: Define plagiarism and explain why paraphrasing with credit avoids it
Paraphrase a real sentence in original wording
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's question and source-evaluation work.
2. Introduce plagiarism and paraphrasing.
3. Have the child paraphrase the coral-bleaching sentence.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's outlining lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: have the child explain the sentence's meaning out loud first, then write down what they just said, rather than trying to paraphrase directly from the text
Ready for more: ask the child why simply changing a few words in a copied sentence still counts as plagiarism
This is a genuinely important academic-integrity skill — take the time needed rather than rushing past it
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended paraphrasing activity — check that the child's version conveys the same meaning (warming oceans cause coral to lose color/bleach) using genuinely different wording and sentence structure, not just synonym-swapping.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 7 Writing standard W.7.8: avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation, continuing this week's research-paper thread.

generationData.instructions: Paraphrase the coral-bleaching sentence in your own words.
